HTTP authorization is network- and Host-based with no application login; local source, scout, and digger files feed an index and browser rendering; media paths invoke urllib, yt-dlp, ffmpeg, and an optional MLT webhook; file-backed state and optional credentials sit under configured runtime directories. Docker binds loopback by default, while a separate live-box recovery script uses passwordless sudo to preserve Tailscale across resets.

Host filesystem roots, downloaded media, and configured media-path confinement.
Server and host availability during source scans, media processing, request-created work, and upstream streams.
The cached Tailscale package, daemon binaries, root state archive, and recovered node identity used by live-box reset recovery.

Unprivileged box account and persistent home storage to passwordless-sudo recovery of root-owned Tailscale software and state; exact sudoers and scheduler configuration are external.
Developer or CI host to third-party browser content loaded by the UI smoke test.

findings.title: Vote restore persists an unvalidated note timestamp into an HTML attribute
findings.summary: An admitted HTTP client can submit a crafted historical vote entry through the undo/restore branch. Unlike normal vote writes, restore_vote does not apply clean_notes, so an attacker-controlled note timestamp is stored and later interpolated without escaping into a data-t attribute in the My votes list. Rendering that list can execute injected markup in another admitted browser.

severity.rationale: The attacker must already be inside an allowed network and a victim must open My votes, but the primitive crosses from ordinary shared-state mutation into persistent script execution in another browser's private application origin.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if the service is shared with mutually untrusted network clients or the origin gains additional browser-held credentials; lower if the deployment is provably single-user.

confidence.rationale: The client-controlled nested notes value is persisted without clean_notes and reaches a quoted attribute in markup assigned through innerHTML; the ordinary write path demonstrates the missing intended validator.

taxonomy.category: Stored browser injection caused by inconsistent nested restore validation

codeEvidence.label: Restore forwards the supplied entry unchanged
codeEvidence.explanation: The restore operation accepts the nested entry object directly and does not call clean_notes.

codeEvidence.label: Nested notes are not normalized before persistence
codeEvidence.explanation: notes is an allowed key, but its member types and timestamp are never checked before entry is written to votes.json.

codeEvidence.label: The intended validator requires a bounded numeric timestamp
codeEvidence.explanation: Normal vote and reason writes call this function; the restore branch is the inconsistent bypass.

codeEvidence.label: Stored timestamp is interpolated unescaped into innerHTML
codeEvidence.explanation: A quote in n.t terminates data-t and can insert an event-bearing element when rowHTML is assigned to #rows.innerHTML.

rootCause.summary: The undo API treats a client-supplied historical object as trusted server state. Its allowlist validates only top-level keys and a few scalar fields, omitting the nested notes schema enforced by normal writes.

findings.remediation: Do not accept a client-supplied vote entry as an undo token. Retain previous state server-side or issue an opaque, integrity-protected reference. If restore remains, reconstruct the entry from explicitly validated fields and run notes through clean_notes before persistence. In the browser, require finite numeric timestamps and create note elements with DOM APIs/textContent/dataset instead of HTML strings. A restrictive script-src CSP adds defense in depth after inline handlers are removed or nonced.

restore_vote persists that value without clean_notes.
The My votes response returns stored notes.

limitations: The application is documented as single-user by default; multi-client deployment determines how often the cross-browser impact is meaningful.

likelihood.rationale: The request is simple for an admitted peer, but deployment is primarily single-user and a victim interaction is required.

findings.title: An unvalidated clip identifier pollutes Object.prototype in browser watch state
findings.summary: The index admits arbitrary string identifiers from already-sent.json, including __proto__, and returns them in queue items. When an invalid item reaches the normal media fallback, wpMark uses the identifier as a key in a plain object. WATCH['__proto__'] resolves Object.prototype, so the fixed watch-state fields are written to the global prototype and inherited by unrelated clip entries.

severity.rationale: The source writer must already control a local shared input and the resulting pollution is limited to fixed client-side watch fields for the lifetime of the page. It can corrupt UI state and destabilize property checks but does not provide arbitrary script execution or server-side state corruption.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if future wpMark call sites permit attacker-selected property names or polluted fields become security decisions; lower to informational if all source writers are fully trusted operators.

confidence.rationale: The special __proto__ lookup semantics, unvalidated source identifier, reachable fallback call, and fixed prototype writes are all explicit in source.

taxonomy.category: Client-side prototype pollution through an unvalidated object key

codeEvidence.explanation: The canonical VK_RE exists but is not applied here, so __proto__ can become an indexed viewkey.

...

    items = [card_of(p['viewkey'], None, cv, ms) for p in backlog_all]
codeEvidence.explanation: An invalid string identifier can reach the browser queue even though mutation APIs later reject it.

codeEvidence.label: Media fallback records the source-derived identifier
codeEvidence.explanation: Invalid IDs cause preview/full API errors and ultimately reach this fallback, which passes viewkey to wpMark.

codeEvidence.label: Plain object indexing reuses Object.prototype

rootCause.summary: Server-side ingestion does not enforce its canonical clip identifier grammar, and client-side per-key state uses a prototype-bearing object without own-property checks.

findings.remediation: Validate every clip identifier with VK_RE while ingesting already-sent and sent-log data, dropping and logging invalid values before index construction. Independently represent WATCH with Map or Object.create(null), validate the parsed localStorage object, and use Object.hasOwn before reusing a keyed record.

findings.title: The UI smoke test renders live third-party content with Chromium's sandbox disabled
findings.summary: tests/parity/ui_queue_smoke.py deliberately drives an unfetchable clip into a live Pornhub embed while launching Chromium with both --no-sandbox and --no-proxy-server. This contradicts the harness's offline isolation claim and exposes the developer or CI account to live third-party browser content without Chromium's normal process sandbox.

severity.rationale: A successful renderer compromise would inherit the test user's host privileges and can affect the workspace or readable credentials, but exploitation requires a browser vulnerability or equivalent compromise in a third-party delivery chain and the smoke test to run.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if the test runs automatically on privileged CI hosts with secrets or writable sensitive mounts; lower if it is always confined to an unprivileged, network-isolated container.

confidence.rationale: The test explicitly waits for Pornhub embed URLs, disables the proxy, disables the browser sandbox, and contains a deterministic fixture that reaches that path.

taxonomy.category: Developer-tool isolation failure for untrusted browser content

codeEvidence.code:

...
- ... `fake_ytdlp/` on `PYTHONPATH` stands in for yt-dlp ...; everything else goes to a dead proxy
codeEvidence.explanation: The documented safety property is local, temporary, and offline execution.

rootCause.summary: The smoke test relies on production's live external-embed fallback while disabling both the browser sandbox and proxy isolation, so its test fixture is not self-contained.

findings.remediation: Remove --no-sandbox for developer-host execution. Block all non-loopback browser egress and replace the third-party embed with a local stub or CDP request interception. If the browser sandbox cannot run in the target environment, execute this test inside a dedicated unprivileged container or VM with no secrets, no sensitive writable mounts, and no Internet access.

findings.title: Namespaced clip metadata controls server-side media destinations without egress validation
findings.summary: For xh: and ep: clips, recursively ingested source_url or url fields become the canonical page URL when they merely start with https://. The application passes that value to yt-dlp, accepts the extractor's HTTP(S) format and playlist URLs without host or address validation, and then fetches them through the full-video proxy, ffmpeg frame extraction, or persistent download path. A source-data writer can therefore induce server-side requests to unintended destinations; automatic preview prewarming supplies a trigger when a poisoned card is displayed.

severity.rationale: The vulnerable server-side egress can reach services unavailable to the source writer and can relay decodable media or consume bandwidth/storage, but exploitation requires write influence over local integration data for a known namespaced clip and useful disclosure depends on yt-dlp/media handling.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if a less-trusted remote scout writes source metadata directly or the host can reach sensitive unauthenticated management services; lower if all source files are generated only by the fully trusted operator and outbound network policy blocks private destinations.

confidence.rationale: The source URL, canonicalization, yt-dlp operand, extracted format acceptance, urllib relay, ffmpeg use, and direct-network fallback are explicit in source. Exact internal-service response disclosure remains target-dependent and is reflected in severity.

taxonomy.category: Server-side request forgery through unvalidated integration metadata

codeEvidence.label: Namespaced source URLs are copied without destination validation
codeEvidence.explanation: Recursive source-file records can supply the server-fetch URL for namespaced identifiers.

codeEvidence.label: The canonical URL control is only a string prefix check
codeEvidence.explanation: Arbitrary HTTPS hosts, ports, credentials, DNS results, and redirects are accepted. The xHamster rewrite changes recognized xHamster hosts but returns all other HTTPS URLs unchanged.

codeEvidence.label: yt-dlp receives the metadata URL and returned media URLs are accepted by protocol only
codeEvidence.explanation: Neither the initial target nor extracted progressive/HLS destinations are constrained to expected public site/CDN hosts or public IP ranges.

codeEvidence.label: Extracted URL is opened and relayed to the client
codeEvidence.code:
rec = resolve_full(vk, force=attempt > 0, fg=True)
f = pick_format(rec, q) if rec.get('url') else None
...
req = urllib.request.Request(f['url'], headers=hdr, method='GET')
try:
    up = phnet.urlopen(req, timeout=20)
codeEvidence.explanation: The media proxy performs a server-side GET to the unchecked extracted URL and later streams its body.

codeEvidence.label: Non-allowlisted hosts bypass the optional proxy and use direct urllib
codeEvidence.explanation: The host suffix list chooses proxy routing; it is not an egress allowlist, so arbitrary metadata-selected hosts are fetched directly.

rootCause.summary: Integration-supplied public display URLs and trusted server-fetch URLs share one field. A startswith('https://') check substitutes for a destination policy, and downstream extractor URLs are trusted solely by protocol.

findings.remediation: Separate display links from trusted server-fetch targets. Construct fetch URLs from validated site plus native identifier wherever possible. When a slug is required, parse the URL and require the exact documented site host or properly delimited site suffix and expected port. Resolve DNS and reject loopback, link-local, private, multicast, and other non-public addresses; repeat validation after every redirect and for every extractor-returned playlist, segment, or format URL. Add network-level egress controls as defense in depth, and rebuild cached indexes after deployment.

page_url_of returns arbitrary HTTPS metadata URLs.
resolve_full passes that URL to yt-dlp.
HTTP(S) format and HLS URLs are accepted without hostname/address validation.
full streaming, frame extraction, and downloads consume the resulting locations.

findings.title: Admitted clients can create unbounded background threads on preview, queue, and webhook paths

findings.title: A box-user-writable cached package is installed and executed as root during reset recovery
findings.summary: scripts/ensure-up.sh trusts the newest filename-matching Tailscale .deb under a directory owned by the unprivileged box account. When a reset removes the system binaries, the recurring recovery workflow installs that local package with sudo apt-get or extracts its binaries and sudo-installs them, then starts tailscaled under sudo. A process that compromises the box account can plant a crafted package and gain root execution at the next recovery.

severity.rationale: Successful exploitation converts box-account code execution into root code execution with complete host impact. It requires control of the box account's persistent directory and the expected reset/missing-binary recovery condition, so attack complexity is elevated.
severity.changeConditions: Raise likelihood if resets are frequent or an attacker can remove the binaries; lower if the external scheduler or sudo policy cannot execute the privileged package/install/start operations shown.

confidence.rationale: The user-writable source, privileged install fallback, root daemon launch, persistence path, and recurring reset workflow are explicit. The exact scheduler identity and sudoers policy are external to the repository, but the script itself requires passwordless sudo and the documented workflow states it runs every 15–30 minutes.

findings.title: Root Tailscale node state is downgraded to box-user-writable persistent storage
findings.summary: The live recovery script uses sudo to archive the root-owned Tailscale state directory, but shell redirection creates state.tgz in the unprivileged box account's persistence directory and chmods it 0600 for that account. severity.rationale: The archive is deliberately sufficient to restore the node without login, so access can outlive the host and affect tailnet identity. confidence.rationale: The root-to-user archive and unauthenticated restore are explicit, and documentation states the archive restores identity without login. Exact clone behavior and tailnet privileges depend on Tailscale state semantics and external ACLs not present in the repository.

findings.title: Malformed or non-regular source files can stall or abort the entire index rebuild
findings.summary: The recursive source scanner opens every matching JSON or saved HTML path without verifying a regular no-follow file, enforcing byte or aggregate limits, or isolating all per-file parsing failures. A source writer can block the rebuild with a FIFO/device or exhaust memory with a large file. Separately, broad glob patterns feed narrower unchecked filename regexes, so a tiny malformed JSON or HTML filename raises before the local error handling and aborts the whole build.

severity.rationale: A writer in the source-integration boundary can deterministically prevent fresh deployments from building an index or leave existing deployments stale using tiny inputs, and can create process-level memory/blocking pressure with special or oversized files. The attacker needs local write influence over SOURCES_DIR.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if a remote automation service can write directly into SOURCES_DIR; lower if the directory is strictly operator-only and all producers enforce regular-file and size constraints externally.

confidence.rationale: The open/read, unchecked regex dereferences, whole-build catch, and missing per-file bounds are explicit in source. Exact memory exhaustion depends on host limits but the tiny filename aborts are deterministic.

rootCause.summary: SOURCES_DIR is treated as a trusted collection instead of a parsing boundary: filename grammar, file type/confinement, resource budgets, and per-file fault isolation are not enforced before blocking reads and regex captures.

findings.remediation: For each candidate path, use lstat/open-no-follow semantics and accept only regular files whose resolved/opened identity remains beneath SOURCES_DIR. Enforce per-file and aggregate byte, record, nesting, string-length, and processing-time budgets before parsing. Validate basenames with fullmatch and check every match before accessing groups. Put all filename parsing and file processing inside a per-file exception boundary so one bad source is skipped and logged. Consider a resource-limited worker for source parsing and commit only a complete validated snapshot.

findings.title: Synthetic range fallback amplifies a one-byte request into up to 32 MiB of upstream reads
findings.summary: When an upstream media server ignores Range and returns 200 with a numeric Content-Length, full_plan synthesizes a 206 response for offsets through 32 MiB. full_chunks implements this by reading and discarding every byte before the requested offset. An admitted client can repeatedly request one byte near the threshold and force roughly 32 MiB of hidden server-side bandwidth and blocking work per response.

severity.rationale: The amplification factor is large and streaming lacks a global byte budget, but exploitation requires an admitted client and a known upstream that ignores Range and supplies a numeric length. Impact is primarily bandwidth and worker degradation on a self-hosted service.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if many supported upstreams ignore Range or the route is exposed to untrusted networks; lower if a reverse proxy globally limits concurrent streams and upstream bytes.

confidence.rationale: The inclusive 32 MiB threshold and discard loop are explicit. Upstream-specific prevalence is unknown and reflected in attack complexity and severity.

codeEvidence.explanation: A request such as bytes=33554432-33554432 produces a one-byte downstream response while setting skip to 32 MiB.

codeEvidence.label: The server reads and discards the complete prefix
codeEvidence.explanation: Discarded upstream bytes are not charged to a global or per-client budget, and the client receives only limit bytes after the skip.

codeEvidence.label: The raw streaming route exposes the skip behavior
codeEvidence.explanation: An admitted HTTP client's Range header directly determines the hidden skip work performed during streaming.

rootCause.summary: The server emulates unsupported upstream seeking by linear prefix discard without accounting for the ratio between downstream response bytes and upstream work.

findings.remediation: Do not synthesize nonzero ranges by linear discard. If upstream ignores a range, return an honest 200, reject the seek with 416/502, or use a bounded local cache designed for random access. If a small fallback is retained, reduce the threshold substantially and enforce global/per-client concurrent-stream and total-upstream-byte budgets based on bytes consumed, not bytes returned.

findings.title: Unbounded fuzzy duplicate matching performs quadratic work on every queue and home request
findings.summary: sent-log titles and collection sizes are unbounded, and suppress_tonight_dups compares every unvoted current-round title against all previously kept titles and recent history using difflib.SequenceMatcher. The queue endpoint performs this from scratch for each request, and home calls queue internally. A source-data writer can supply many long, equal-length, nonmatching titles and make ordinary or repeated admitted requests consume superlinear CPU.

severity.rationale: The algorithm is persistent on common read paths and attacker-controlled title length multiplies the all-pairs cost, allowing service-level CPU denial. The attacker must influence authoritative source data; request amplification then requires only admitted client access or normal page loads.
severity.changeConditions: Raise if remote automation can write sent-log directly or production rounds are large; lower if trusted producers enforce strict record/title limits and a front proxy rate-limits reads.

confidence.rationale: The nested comparisons, SequenceMatcher call, unbounded title normalization, and per-request queue/home call sites are explicit. Exact exhaustion thresholds depend on hardware and dataset shape.

taxonomy.category: Algorithmic-complexity denial of service in source-driven request processing

codeEvidence.label: Long source-controlled titles reach SequenceMatcher
codeEvidence.code:
def normalize_title(t):
    if not isinstance(t, str): return ''
    s = t.lower()
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9\s]+', ' ', s)
    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()
...
def title_near_dup(a, b, ratio=DUP_TITLE_RATIO):
    if not a or not b: return False
    if a == b: return True
    if abs(len(a) - len(b)) > max(12, int(0.4 * max(len(a), len(b)))): return False
    return difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio() >= ratio
codeEvidence.explanation: No title-length budget precedes the fuzzy matcher; equal-length nonmatching titles bypass the only cheap length rejection.

codeEvidence.label: Each current title scans all kept and recent titles
codeEvidence.explanation: For unique nonmatching titles, seen_titles grows on every iteration and the first nested loop performs approximately N²/2 fuzzy comparisons, plus recent-history comparisons.

codeEvidence.label: Every queue request runs duplicate suppression
codeEvidence.code:
def queue(mode):
    votes = read_votes(); ...
    tn, info = tonight_round()
    ...
    tn_raw_n = len(tn)
    tn, dup_suppressed = suppress_tonight_dups(tn, {vk for vk, _ in tn if voted(vk)})
codeEvidence.explanation: There is no cache keyed by source version, comparison budget, or background precomputation.

codeEvidence.label: The dashboard duplicates the same request-path work
codeEvidence.explanation: Both /api/queue and /api/home expose the unbounded algorithm on normal page/dashboard reads.

rootCause.summary: Fuzzy deduplication operates directly over unbounded source collections and strings on synchronous request paths, without precomputation, indexing, caching, or a work budget.

findings.remediation: Cap accepted title length and current/recent record counts at ingestion. Precompute normalized titles when the index changes and cache suppression results by the sent-log/index version. Replace all-pairs SequenceMatcher with bounded candidate buckets or fingerprints, apply a strict comparison/time budget, and fall back to exact matching when exhausted. Perform expensive refresh work outside request handlers.

candidate.security_invariant: Only explicitly authenticated principals may read private data or invoke sensitive operations.
candidate.source_to_sink: Compose allowlists broad bridge/private ranges because Docker rewrites source addresses; documentation permits 0.0.0.0 publication; middleware checks only source IP and caller Host, while direct clients can forge matching Origin and reach all APIs.
candidate.impact: Remote peer can read private adult-viewing state, mutate ratings/highlights, trigger downloads, and use configured Pornhub favorite authority.
supporting_source_evidence: Compose explicitly allows RFC1918 bridge/private ranges.
README permits 0.0.0.0 for remote use.
Guards do not authenticate identity.
Direct clients can supply Content-Type/Origin/Host.
counterevidence: Binding exact Tailscale address narrows exposure.
Host/Origin controls protect browser request integrity but not direct-client authentication.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Keep loopback/specific tailnet binding, remove broad ranges, use authenticated proxy/Tailscale Serve, and authenticate all private/sensitive APIs.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-egress-full-ssrf
surfaces.notes: This candidate is a duplicate operation of the validated source-metadata SSRF root control and is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Namespaced clip metadata can turn the full-video proxy into an SSRF response oracle
candidate.rule: Only site-owned, publicly routable media URLs may reach yt-dlp or the streaming proxy.
candidate.attacker: An actor able to alter source JSON for a known namespaced clip and induce an admitted client to resolve it.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Read-only source metadata must not select arbitrary server-side network destinations or expose their responses.
candidate.source_to_sink: build_index copies source_url/url; ph_page_url selects it; page_url_of accepts any https:// string; resolve_full gives it to yt-dlp; extracted HTTP(S) URLs are accepted by protocol only; /media/full opens and streams the result without host/address/redirect checks.
candidate.concrete_impact: Server can connect to HTTPS services on loopback/private/link-local networks and may relay media bytes or expose timing/error behavior.
supporting_source_evidence: Only startswith('https://') constrains metadata URLs.
Extracted format host/address/redirect relation is not checked.
full_plan opens f.url and full_chunks relays its body.
counterevidence: Useful exfiltration generally requires a target yt-dlp recognizes as media.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Derive canonical per-site URLs or enforce per-site host and public-address allowlists before every yt-dlp/urllib/ffmpeg request and after redirects.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-egress-download-ssrf
surfaces.notes: The unchecked-destination dataflow is merged into the validated source-metadata SSRF finding. Its separate no-quota observation does not establish a distinct authority gain: downloads are an admitted-client operation with one global active-job cap, so it remains hardening guidance.

candidate.title: Namespaced download jobs fetch arbitrary metadata-selected URLs and have no size or wall-clock quota
candidate.rule: Download jobs must use validated site URLs and bounded resource budgets.
candidate.attacker: An admitted HTTP client acting on a namespaced clip with attacker-selected source metadata.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: A download request must not access unintended destinations or consume unbounded storage.
candidate.source_to_sink: The arbitrary metadata URL is the final yt-dlp operand and its output is persisted; one-job concurrency exists but there is no filesize, quota, or total process deadline.
candidate.concrete_impact: Internal requests and persistent media writes; large or indefinite responses can fill DOWNLOAD_ROOT or monopolize downloads.
supporting_source_evidence: Non-walled URLs route directly.
stdout loop can remain active indefinitely.
No filesize/duration/disk quota.
counterevidence: Completed downloads are not served by this code.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Validate destinations and add filesize, duration, subprocess, free-space, and aggregate-root quotas.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-egress-ffmpeg-ssrf
surfaces.notes: This candidate is a duplicate operation of the validated source-metadata SSRF root control and is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Extracted HLS and progressive URLs reach ffmpeg without egress validation
candidate.rule: Media URLs handed to native decoders must pass the same destination policy as initial URLs.
candidate.attacker: An actor controlling namespaced source metadata or its extraction page.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Native processing must not connect to arbitrary destinations selected by metadata.
candidate.source_to_sink: resolve_full retains unchecked progressive/HLS URLs from yt-dlp; user_frame and _extract_frames pass them to ffmpeg; playlist, redirect, segment host and addresses are not checked.
candidate.concrete_impact: Internal playlists, segments, or media may be fetched and decodable content converted to browser-visible JPEGs.
supporting_source_evidence: HLS selection checks protocol text only.
ffmpeg receives f.url directly.
Timeouts do not prevent unintended egress.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Enforce expected public destinations for playlists, redirects, and segments through a policy proxy.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-baseline-ssrf
surfaces.notes: This candidate is a duplicate operation of the validated source-metadata SSRF root control and is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Scout-controlled source URLs are dereferenced without SSRF-safe egress validation
candidate.attacker: A malicious/compromised scout or attacker poisoning SOURCES_DIR metadata for a namespaced clip.
candidate.security_invariant: Metadata integrations must not cause arbitrary internal or non-approved network requests.
candidate.source_to_sink: Index copies source_url/url, page_url_of accepts any https:// text, ph_page_url returns it, yt-dlp follows it and emits further URLs, and full_plan opens the emitted URL without destination validation.
candidate.impact: Internal probing and possible retrieval/streaming of internal resources plus bandwidth abuse.
supporting_source_evidence: Recursive JSON ingestion retains URLs.
startswith https is the entire decision.
yt-dlp and urllib dereference unchecked destinations.
counterevidence: Ordinary HTTP clients cannot set source_url.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Canonicalize per-site URLs or strictly validate hostname, port, resolved address, redirects, and every extracted URL; add egress firewall.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-egress-preview-thread-dos
surfaces.notes: This operation shares the validated unbounded request-triggered raw-thread control failure and bounded-executor remediation; it is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Uncached preview requests create an unbounded number of background threads
candidate.rule: Expensive background work must be deduplicated and use a bounded executor.
candidate.attacker: Any admitted HTTP client with a known clip ID.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: A client must not allocate unbounded threads by repeating a pending preview.
candidate.source_to_sink: fetch=False lacks an in-flight marker; api_preview calls prefetch_preview, which creates a raw Thread for every request; the per-viewkey lock then makes duplicates wait.
candidate.concrete_impact: Thousands of waiting threads can exhaust memory/scheduler/process limits.
supporting_source_evidence: No queue, executor, pending set, or limit.
fetch=False cannot distinguish pending.
Network timeouts make accumulation practical.
counterevidence: Requires admitted client and known clip.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Single-flight Future per key plus bounded executor/queue and throttling.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-http-queue-thread-dos
surfaces.notes: This operation shares the validated unbounded request-triggered raw-thread control failure and bounded-executor remediation; it is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Queue and home reads spawn unbounded sweep threads and duplicate uncached upstream lookups
candidate.rule: Coalesce cache misses and cap request-triggered background sweeps
candidate.attacker: An HTTP client admitted by ALLOWED_NETS
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Read endpoints must not amplify requests into unbounded local threads and upstream work.
candidate.source_to_sink: Both /api/queue and /api/home call queue(); when activity data is uncached queue starts one raw thread per request for up to 30 clips. clip_info has no per-viewkey in-flight lock, so concurrent sweeps duplicate remote API calls.
candidate.concrete_impact: Cold-cache request bursts can create unbounded threads and duplicate upstream traffic, denying service.
supporting_source_evidence: app/index.py:813-818 starts a raw thread per request.
app/clips.py:333-355 releases the dictionary lock before duplicate network lookups.
counterevidence: Each sweep is capped at 30 clips and warm results are cached.
Attacker must be an admitted client.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Use a bounded shared executor, a global pending-viewkey set, per-viewkey single-flight, and endpoint throttling.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-egress-mlt-thread-dos
surfaces.notes: This operation shares the validated unbounded request-triggered raw-thread control failure and bounded-executor remediation; it is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Repeated MLT requests spawn unbounded authenticated webhook threads
candidate.rule: Webhook delivery must be queued, deduplicated, and concurrency-bounded.
candidate.attacker: Any admitted HTTP client when MLT webhook URL/key are configured.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: A shared client must not create unbounded threads or flood an authenticated downstream endpoint.
candidate.source_to_sink: Each on=true POST can create a wake and new raw daemon thread; open entries are not deduplicated for delivery; each thread blocks up to eight seconds and sends both credentials.
candidate.concrete_impact: Local thread/socket exhaustion and authenticated downstream request floods.
supporting_source_evidence: Already-open entries still create wakes.
One thread per accepted request.
State lock does not bound deliveries.
counterevidence: POST guarded and known clip required.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Bound/coalesce delivery queue, idempotency/resend interval, backoff, queue cap, and client rate limits.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-deploy-state-restore
surfaces.notes: The untrusted restore direction shares the same box-user-writable Tailscale persistence boundary and root-owned-storage remediation as the validated node-state exposure finding. It is merged there rather than counted separately; no archive-based root code execution was established.

candidate.title: User-writable Tailscale state is restored into the root daemon without authenticity protection
candidate.attacker: A malicious process running as the box account that can replace state.tgz before reset.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Only root-trusted state may determine the privileged daemon's identity and network membership.
candidate.source_to_sink_explanation: A nonempty user-writable state.tgz is sudo-extracted into /var/lib/tailscale, chowned root, and used by root tailscaled with no integrity or identity check.
candidate.concrete_impact: A same-user attacker can cause the privileged daemon to adopt an attacker-selected valid identity after reset, potentially changing service reachability.
supporting_source_evidence: Archive can restore a complete node identity without login.
The app has no login and relies on network/Host checks.
Reset recovery is an expected workflow.
counterevidence: Requires same-account execution, a valid replacement state, and later recovery.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Move backups to root-owned authenticated storage and validate expected machine identity before daemon start.

surfaces.label: Candidate disposition: cand-ingestion-dated-name-dos
surfaces.notes: The malformed-filename rebuild abort is one manifestation of the validated source-scanner validation and per-file isolation failure and is merged into that finding rather than counted separately.

candidate.title: Malformed dated-list filenames abort the complete index rebuild
candidate.rule: Validate filename matches before capture access and isolate file failures
candidate.attacker: A writer able to add a JSON file under SOURCES_DIR.
candidate.source_to_sink: Broad globs match filenames whose narrower date regex returns no match; unchecked .group() aborts build_index.
candidate.concrete_impact: A tiny malformed file prevents fresh index construction or leaves an existing index stale.
counterevidence: An existing cache remains usable but stale.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Check regex matches and skip malformed files inside per-file exception boundaries.

candidate.attacker: A writer able to add a saved HTML page under SOURCES_DIR.
